concepts.name: Origin and Institutional Framework of EoDB Index
key_dimensions: Published by World Bank Group — NOT IMF or WEF (common UPSC trap)
Discontinued in 2021 after data irregularities scandal involving senior World Bank officials
Replaced by Business Ready (B-READY) Index launched in 2024
Distinction between Doing Business Report and other World Bank flagship reports (WDR, WDI)

concepts.name: Discontinuation of EoDB and the Data Manipulation Controversy
key_dimensions: World Bank halted the report in September 2021 citing irregularities in 2018 and 2020 editions
Countries alleged to have benefited from manipulated data: China, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Azerbaijan
Involvement of then-World Bank President David Malpass and Christine Lagarde (IMF) controversy
Institutional credibility implications for multilateral bodies and index-based policymaking

concepts.name: Business Ready (B-READY) Index: Successor to EoDB
key_dimensions: Launched by World Bank in 2024 as a replacement for Doing Business Index
Covers 3 pillars: Regulatory Framework, Public Services, Operational Efficiency
Evaluates 10 topic areas aligned with the business lifecycle
Key difference from EoDB: incorporates quality of regulation, not just ease/speed — avoids 'race to the bottom' critique

concepts.name: Methodology of EoDB Index: Parameters and Weighting
key_dimensions: 10 parameters including Starting a Business, Dealing with Construction Permits, Getting Electricity, Registering Property, Getting Credit, Protecting Minority Investors, Paying Taxes, Trading Across Borders, Enforcing Contracts, Resolving Insolvency
Distance to Frontier (DTF) score used — measures absolute performance, not relative ranking alone
Equal weighting to all 10 parameters — a common trap (no parameter has higher weight)
Survey-based methodology using standardized 'case study' firms — not actual business data

concepts.name: India's EoDB Ranking Trajectory and Key Milestones
key_dimensions: India's rank improved from 142 (2014) to 63 (2020) — a jump of 79 positions in 6 years
India among top 10 improvers for three consecutive years: 2016, 2017, 2018
Best rank achieved: 63 in Doing Business Report 2020 (DB2020)
Cities surveyed for India: Mumbai and Delhi (NOT all metros — UPSC trap)

concepts.name: Parameters Where India Performed Best vs Worst
key_dimensions: Strong performance: Getting Credit (rank 25), Protecting Minority Investors (rank 13 in DB2020)
Weak performance: Enforcing Contracts (rank 163), Trading Across Borders (historically poor)
Resolving Insolvency improved significantly after IBC 2016 — from 136 to 52
Starting a Business remained a challenge despite SPICe+ reforms

concepts.name: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016 and EoDB Linkage
key_dimensions: IBC directly improved 'Resolving Insolvency' parameter — rank jumped from 136 (2017) to 52 (2020)
IBC reduced average insolvency resolution time from 4.3 years to under 2 years (target 180/270 days)
Recovery rate improved from ~26 cents to ~71 cents on the dollar
NCLT/NCLAT as institutional infrastructure — linkage to EoDB improvements

concepts.name: Reforms Under 'Getting Credit' Parameter
key_dimensions: India ranked 25 globally in Getting Credit (DB2020) — one of the best parameters
Secured Transactions Law reforms: SARFAESI Act amendments, creation of CERSAI registry
Credit Information Bureau (CIBIL) and expansion of credit bureau coverage
Distinction between 'Strength of Legal Rights Index' and 'Depth of Credit Information Index' — two sub-components

concepts.name: Enforcing Contracts Parameter: India's Persistent Challenge
key_dimensions: India ranked 163 out of 190 in Enforcing Contracts (DB2020) — worst performing parameter
Average time to enforce a contract in India: ~1,445 days (global average ~589 days)
Commercial Courts Act 2015 created to address this — limited impact on rank
UPSC trap: Arbitration and Conciliation Act amendments aim to improve this but survey measures court-based enforcement only

concepts.name: DPIIT's Role in EoDB Reforms and Coordination
key_dimensions: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for EoDB in India
Launched Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) for states — linked to EoDB framework
DPIIT coordinates with 16+ ministries/departments for reform implementation
Distinction: DPIIT handles EoDB; Ministry of Finance handles Fiscal/Tax reforms separately

concepts.name: State-Level EoDB Rankings: Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP)
key_dimensions: DPIIT ranks Indian states on EoDB through BRAP — separate from World Bank's global index
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana were top performers in early BRAP editions
2022 BRAP: Top performers included Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
BRAP covers 301 reform points across 15 business regulatory areas — much more granular than World Bank index

concepts.name: Single Window Clearance Systems and EoDB
key_dimensions: National Single Window System (NSWS) launched in 2021 — 'Invest India' portal integration
Addresses 'Starting a Business' and 'Construction Permits' parameters
SPICe+ (Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus) — integrated MCA portal
UPSC trap: NSWS is different from state-level single windows; national system does NOT replace state portals

concepts.name: Trading Across Borders Parameter and India's Reforms
key_dimensions: Historically one of India's weakest parameters — time and cost of exports/imports
SWIFT (Single Window Interface for Facilitating Trade) at customs — key reform
Nhava Sheva (JNPT) and Chennai ports used as reference points in World Bank survey
PCS1x (Port Community System) and FASTag at ports — digitization of trade logistics

concepts.name: Protecting Minority Investors: India's Strongest Parameter
key_dimensions: India ranked 13 globally in Protecting Minority Investors (DB2020)
Companies Act 2013 amendments: related party transactions disclosure, class action suits
SEBI regulations on insider trading and disclosure norms contribute to this parameter
Sub-indices: Extent of Disclosure Index, Director Liability Index, Shareholder Suits Index — UPSC may ask about specific components

concepts.name: Paying Taxes Parameter: GST's Impact on EoDB
key_dimensions: GST (2017) subsumed 17 central and state taxes — reduced number of tax payments
India's rank in Paying Taxes improved but remains moderate (~115 in DB2020)
UPSC trap: GST improved tax compliance ease but compliance hours initially increased due to multiple returns (GSTR-1, 3B, annual)
E-filing, pre-filled returns, and GST Council rationalization as ongoing reforms

concepts.name: Critique and Limitations of EoDB Index
key_dimensions: Covers only 2 cities per large country (Delhi and Mumbai for India) — not representative
Measures 'de jure' regulations, not 'de facto' implementation on ground
Focuses on small-medium domestic firms — ignores FDI-related barriers and large infrastructure projects
Does not measure labor market flexibility, environmental regulations, or corruption levels — key for actual business climate

concepts.name: EoDB vs Other Business Climate Indices: Key Distinctions
key_dimensions: WEF Global Competitiveness Index (GCI): broader, includes innovation, institutions, infrastructure — NOT just regulatory ease
World Bank EoDB: regulatory processes for a small domestic firm — narrow focus
UNCTAD World Investment Report: focuses on FDI flows, not regulatory ease
Heritage Foundation Index of Economic Freedom: includes rule of law, government size — different dimensions

concepts.name: FDI Inflows and EoDB Correlation: India's Experience
key_dimensions: India's FDI inflows increased alongside EoDB rank improvement (2014–2020 period)
However, correlation ≠ causation — PLI schemes, market size also drove FDI
UPSC trap: India's highest ever FDI ($81.97 billion in 2020-21) came despite rank stagnation
Sectoral FDI data from DPIIT vs RBI — two different counting methodologies

concepts.name: Labor Law Reforms and EoDB: The Missing Dimension
key_dimensions: EoDB index does NOT include a dedicated labor regulation parameter — UPSC trap
India's 4 Labor Codes (2019-2020) consolidating 44 central laws not captured in EoDB ranking
World Bank's separate 'Women, Business and the Law' index covers gender-specific employment regulations
Labour codes address 'employing workers' — a parameter World Bank removed from EoDB ranking calculation in 2009

concepts.name: Decriminalization of Minor Offences and EoDB Reforms
key_dimensions: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2023: decriminalized 183 provisions across 42 Acts
Targets 'Starting a Business' and 'Dealing with Permits' parameters — reduces fear of prosecution
Companies Act amendments: removed imprisonment for minor procedural violations
Distinction: decriminalization ≠ deregulation — penalties (fines) still exist, only criminal liability removed
